theorem.statement:
The full incompressible-rigidity question has an affirmative answer.  For every fixed bounded class \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\), there is \(C<\infty\) such that every aligned pair with \(\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq1\) obeys
\[
 d_Q(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
 \leq C\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
 \leq C\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}.
\]
Consequently, on every fixed nondegenerate class containing the Hamiltonian lower family,
\[
 \Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\asymp
 \Omega^Q_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\asymp
 \varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}
\]
for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\).  In the primary two-node \(C^2\) Morse class the exponent is \(3/4\).
theorem.proof_tex:
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}type\text{-}incompressible\text{-}rigidity}\) gives the two residual inequalities for arbitrary admissible DAGs, mechanisms, and decoders.  With the full-law residual reduction,
\[
 d_Q(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
 \leq C\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}
 \leq C'D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}.
\tag{1}
\]
Canonical encoder invariance gives the same upper bound for \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\).  Taking suprema proves both upper moduli.

The localized lower theorem gives
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta_0,\theta_h)\geq c h^{k+1},
 \qquad D_H(\theta_0,\theta_h)\leq C h^{k+m+1}.
\tag{2}
\]
Since \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\leq C d_Q\), (2) also lower-bounds \(d_Q\).  Lower-family membership places both models in the unchanged full class.  Taking \(h=(\varepsilon/C)^{1/(k+m+1)}\) proves both lower bounds.

For \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\),
\[
 \frac{k+1}{k+m+1}=\frac34.
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:primary\text{-}morse\text{-}nonlinear\text{-}incompressible\text{-}rigidity}\) proves this specialization, while Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:primary\text{-}morse\text{-}audit}\) gives its positive lower coefficient.
theorem.justification: This theorem closes the determinant-assisted arbitrary-map rigidity problem and turns the lower obstruction into the sharp full-class modulus.
theorem.gap: The prior gap was the weighted strip-to-corner estimate for arbitrary approximately incompressible maps; the proof resolves it by finite Taylor-jet elimination with the determinant equation retained.
theorem.consumer: Population recovery, certified estimation, and quotient confidence diameters may now use the sharp exponent.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(w_i\in C^{k-1}(\mathbb T)\), \(i\in[n]\), satisfy \(\lVert w_i\rVert_{C^{k-1}}\leq K\), have zero set \(Z_i\) of cardinality at most \(J\), have distinct zeros separated by at least \(\Delta _0\), and obey
\[
 |w_i(t)|\geq a_0\operatorname {dist}_{\mathbb T}(t,Z_i)^m,
 \qquad 1\leq m\leq k-1.
\]
For \(v\in C^k(\mathbb T^n;\mathbb R^n)\), put
\[
 A_i v_i(t)=\int_{\mathbb T^{n-1}}v_i(t,z_{-i})\,d\lambda^{n-1}(z_{-i}),
 \qquad Q_i v_i=v_i-A_i v_i,
\]
and
\[
 {\cal R}_w(v)=\lVert\operatorname {div}v\rVert_{H^{-1}(\mathbb T^n)}+
 \left\{\sum_{i=1}^n\lVert w_iQ_iv_i\rVert_{L^2(\lambda^n)}^2\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
There are constants \(C<\infty\) and \(h_0>0\), depending only on \((n,k,m,a_0,J,\Delta _0,K)\), such that, for \(0<h\leq h_0\),
\[
 \left\{\sum_{i=1}^n\lVert Q_iv_i\rVert_2^2\right\}^{1/2}
 \leq C\left\{h^{-m}{\cal R}_w(v)+h^{k+1}\lVert v\rVert_{C^k}\right\}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We prove the estimate rather than invoke an elliptic or Hodge endpoint theorem.  Write \(U_i(h)=\{t:\operatorname {dist}_{\mathbb T}(t,Z_i)<h\}\), where
\[
 0<h\leq h_0:=\min\{1,\Delta _0/8\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The components of \(U_i(2h)\) are disjoint.  The finite-type lower bound gives
\[
 \lVert {\bf1}_{\{z_i\notin U_i(h)\}}Q_iv_i\rVert_2
 \leq a_0^{-1}h^{-m}\lVert w_iQ_iv_i\rVert_2.
\tag{2}
\]
Subdivide every circle coordinate into intervals of length between \(h/2\) and \(h\), with interval endpoints chosen to respect the components of \(U_i(2h)\).  On each resulting \(n\)-dimensional product box \(Q\), take the Taylor polynomial \(P_Qv\) of total degree at most \(k-1\) at its center.  Taylor's formula with integral remainder and \(\lVert v\rVert_{C^k}=B\) gives
\[
 \lVert v-P_Qv\rVert_{L^2(Q)}
 \leq C B h^k\lambda^n(Q)^{1/2}
 \leq C B h^{k+n/2}.
\tag{3}
\]

Write
\[
 (P_Qv)_i(x)=\sum_{|\nu|\leq k-1}c_{i,\nu}(Q)(x-x_Q)^\nu.
\tag{4}
\]
After rescaling a box to \((-1,1)^d\), the functional
\[
 P\longmapsto \lVert s^mP\rVert_{L^2(-1,1)^d}
\tag{5}
\]
is a norm on polynomials of degree at most \(k-1\): zero norm makes \(P\) vanish on an open set and hence makes every coefficient zero.  Compactness of the Euclidean unit sphere of coefficients gives a finite inverse constant depending only on \((k,m)\).  Thus (2) controls all coefficients of (4) on boxes outside the corresponding critical strip.

For adjacent boxes, Taylor's formula gives
\[
 c_{i,\nu}(Q')-c_{i,\nu}(Q)
 =\sum_{r=1}^{k-1-|\nu|}
   \frac{(x_{Q'}-x_Q)^r}{r!}c_{i,\nu+r e_j}(Q)
   +\rho_{i,\nu}(Q,Q'),
 \qquad
 |\rho_{i,\nu}(Q,Q')|\leq C B h^{k-|\nu|}.
\tag{6}
\]
The coefficient of \((x-x_Q)^\nu\) in the divergence equation is
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^n(\nu_i+1)c_{i,\nu+e_i}(Q)=d_\nu(Q),
\tag{7}
\]
where testing against rescaled monomials bounds the collection \(d_\nu(Q)\) by \(C\lVert\operatorname {div}v\rVert_{H^{-1}(Q)}\).  Equations (6)--(7) give a finite recurrence.  A coefficient of component \(i\) entering an \(i\)-strip either reaches an annular box controlled by (5), or (7) transfers it to a component \(j\neq i\).  The latter coefficient is controlled unless the box also meets a \(j\)-strip.  Each transfer lowers the degree in the entering coordinate, so after at most \(k\) transfers the only uncontrolled boxes meet two critical strips.

Summing the recurrence creates no factor equal to the number of boxes: every interior face in (6) occurs twice with opposite signs and periodicity cancels terminal faces.  The degree-zero coefficient surviving the telescoping is precisely \(A_iv_i\), which \(Q_i\) removes.  Therefore
\[
 \sum_i\lVert Q_iv_i\rVert_2
 \leq C h^{-m}{\cal R}_w(v)
 +C\left\{\sum_{i\neq j}\sum_{z\in Z_i,z'\in Z_j}
   \sum_{Q\subset\{|x_i-z|<2h,\ |x_j-z'|<2h\}}
   \lVert v-P_Qv\rVert_{L^2(Q)}^2\right\}^{1/2},
\tag{8}
\]
where the inner sum ranges over the product boxes \(Q\subset\{|x_i-z|<2h,|x_j-z'|<2h\}\).  For fixed \((i,j,z,z')\), there are at most \(C h^{-(n-2)}\) such boxes.  Applying (3) and summing their squared remainders gives
\[
 \left\{\sum_{i\neq j}\sum_{z,z'}\sum_Q
   \lVert v-P_Qv\rVert_{L^2(Q)}^2\right\}^{1/2}
 \leq C B\{h^{-(n-2)}h^{2k+n}\}^{1/2}
 =C B h^{k+1}.
\tag{9}
\]
Combining (8)--(9) proves the claim.  The power \(h^{k+1}\) is the product of a \(C^k\) Taylor remainder of size \(h^k\) and the square root \(h\) of the two-dimensional critical volume.  No endpoint bound for a Hodge projection is used.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the primary case \(n=2\), \(k=2\), and \(m=1\), let \(w_i\in C^1(\mathbb T)\) have at most \(J\) separated zeros and satisfy \(|w_i(t)|\geq a_0\operatorname {dist}_{\mathbb T}(t,Z_i)\).  For every periodic \(v\in C^2(\mathbb T^2;\mathbb R^2)\), after subtracting the coordinatewise fiber means, put
\[
 E_{\rm lin}(v)=\lVert\operatorname {div}v\rVert_2+
 \left(\lVert w_1v_1\rVert_2^2+\lVert w_2v_2\rVert_2^2\right)^{1/2},
 \qquad B=\lVert v\rVert_{C^2}.
\]
Then, uniformly for \(0<h\leq h_0\),
\[
 \lVert v\rVert_2\leq C\{E_{\rm lin}(v)/h+Bh^3\}.
\]
Consequently, if \(E_{\rm lin}(v)\leq Bh_0^4\),
\[
 \lVert v\rVert_2\leq C B^{1/4}E_{\rm lin}(v)^{3/4}.
\]
For \(V=\operatorname {id}+v\), the exact identity
\[
 \operatorname {div}v=\det DV-1-\det Dv
\]
records the determinant defect retained in the nonlinear argument.  The estimate applies to every normalized divergence-free periodic \(C^2\) field, not merely radial fields.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Apply Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}type\text{-}solenoidal\text{-}strip\text{-}interpolation}\) with \(n=2\), \(k=2\), and \(m=1\).  Since \(\lVert g\rVert_{H^{-1}}\leq\lVert g\rVert_2\),
\[
 \lVert v\rVert_2\leq C\{h^{-1}E_{\rm lin}(v)+Bh^3\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The fiber-mean normalization says \(A_iv_i=0\), so the cited lemma's left side is \(\lVert v\rVert_2\).  If \(0<E_{\rm lin}(v)\leq Bh_0^4\), take
\[
 h=\{E_{\rm lin}(v)/B\}^{1/4}.
\tag{2}
\]
Both terms in (1) equal \(B^{1/4}E_{\rm lin}(v)^{3/4}\).  If \(E_{\rm lin}(v)=0\), let \(h\downarrow0\) in (1).

Direct expansion in two dimensions gives
\[
 \det(I+Dv)=1+\partial_1v_1+\partial_2v_2+
 \partial_1v_1\partial_2v_2-
 \partial_2v_1\partial_1v_2
 =1+\operatorname {div}v+\det Dv.
\tag{3}
\]
Rearranging proves the determinant identity and completes the proof.

added_lemmas.statement:
The canonical encoder orbit \([g_\theta]_{\mathfrak S_n\ltimes\operatorname {Isom}(\mathbb T)^n}\) is invariant under every coordinatewise circular latent reparameterization, including orientation reversal.  Moreover \(d_Q\) is an intrinsic symmetric orbit distance, and on the bounded model class
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq C d_Q(\theta,\widetilde\theta).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For one coordinate let \(x'=\psi(x)\), where \(\psi\) is any circle diffeomorphism.  Let \(q^0d\lambda\) and \(q^{0\prime}d\lambda\) be the same baseline law, and let \(\beta,\beta'\) be the two probability-integral gauges.  Both \(\beta\) and \(\beta'\circ\psi\) push \(q^0d\lambda\) to \(\lambda\).  Hence
\[
 I=(\beta'\circ\psi)\circ\beta^{-1}
\tag{1}
\]
preserves \(\lambda\).  Thus \(|I'|=1\), its derivative has constant sign, and \(I(t)=t+c\) or \(I(t)=-t+c\) modulo \(2\pi\).  Since \(h'=\psi\circ h\),
\[
 g'=\beta'\circ h'=I\circ\beta\circ h=I\circ g.
\tag{2}
\]
Applying (2) coordinatewise and allowing one common permutation proves invariance.

The finite permutation group and the compact circle-isometry group act isometrically on \(L^2(\lambda^n;\mathbb T^n)\).  Inversion gives symmetry, composition plus Minkowski gives the triangle inequality, and compactness makes the infimum attained.

For a canonical alignment define
\[
 \phi_i=\beta_{\theta i}^{-1}\circ I_i\circ\beta_{\widetilde\theta,\pi(i)}.
\tag{3}
\]
Integrating the positive perfect-intervention density over the coordinates other than \(i\) gives its \(i\)-th marginal \(q_i^0\).  The density bounds therefore give class-uniform positive lower and upper bounds for \(q_i^0\), hence a class-uniform Lipschitz bound for \(\beta_{\theta i}^{-1}\).  They and decoder conditioning also bound the density of \(\bar P_\theta\) relative to \(\lambda^n\).  Applying these bounds to the two auxiliary directed losses and taking infima proves
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq C d_Q(\theta,\widetilde\theta).
\tag{4}
\]
This is only a one-way comparison and does not characterize the zero set of the auxiliary discrepancy.

added_lemmas.statement:
There is a class-uniform constant \(C<\infty\) such that every aligned pair \(\theta,\widetilde\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) with \(\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq1\) satisfies, for \(0<h\leq h_0\),
\[
 d_Q(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
 \leq C\{\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)/h^m+h^{k+1}\}.
\]
Hence
\[
 d_Q(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
 \leq C\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)},
 \qquad
 d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
 \leq C\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}.
\]
The constants are uniform over both models' DAGs, all admissible mechanisms, and all admissible decoders; no radial, near-isometric, or common-mechanism restriction is imposed.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix the group permutation used in Definition \(\mathrm{def:analytic\text{-}residual}\), and abbreviate \(T=T_{\theta,\widetilde\theta}\), \(R_i=r_{\theta i}\circ\beta_{\theta i}^{-1}\), \(S_i=r_{\widetilde\theta,\pi(i)}\circ\beta_{\widetilde\theta,\pi(i)}^{-1}\), and \(E=\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\).  By the perfect-intervention factorization, integration in reverse topological order gives
\[
 q_i^e(t)=\int_{\mathbb T^{n-1}}p_\theta^{i,e}(t,x_{-i})\,d\lambda^{n-1}(x_{-i}).
\tag{1}
\]
The density bounds and density smoothness therefore give uniform positive lower, upper, and \(C^k\) bounds for \(q_i^e\).  Differentiation gives uniform \(C^k\) bounds for \(R_i,S_i\) and uniform conditioning of every \(\beta_i^{\pm1}\).  In particular,
\[
 R_i'(u)=\frac{r_{\theta i}'(\beta_{\theta i}^{-1}(u))}
 {q_i^0(\beta_{\theta i}^{-1}(u))}.
\]
The bi-Lipschitz bounds for \(\beta_i\) therefore transport the finite-type margin and critical separation to \(R_i,S_i\), with class-uniform modified constants.  Decoder smoothness and conditioning give the corresponding bounds for \(T,T^{-1}\).

Put
\[
 e_0=|\det DT|-1,\qquad e_i=R_i\circ T_i-S_i.
\tag{2}
\]
These functions have uniformly bounded first derivatives and their \(L^2\) norms have Euclidean sum at most \(E\).  If a Lipschitz function \(u\) has supremum \(M\), it has magnitude at least \(M/2\) on a ball of radius \(M/(2L)\).  The volume of that ball proves
\[
 \max_{0\leq i\leq n}\lVert e_i\rVert_\infty
 \leq C E^{2/(n+2)}=:\eta_E.
\tag{3}
\]

For fixed \(z_i\), the image of the connected transverse torus under \(z_{-i}\mapsto T_i(z_i,z_{-i})\) is a connected arc.  If its length is \(\ell\leq\pi\), removal of at most \(J\) critical points leaves a subarc of length at least \(\ell/(J+1)\).  On the middle half the finite-type profile has constant derivative sign and
\[
 |R_i'(t)|\geq a_0\{\ell/(4J+4)\}^m.
\]
Integration and (3) yield
\[
 c\ell^{m+1}\leq\operatorname {osc}R_i\leq2\eta_E,
\qquad
 \operatorname {diam}T_i(\{z_i\}\times\mathbb T^{n-1})
 \leq C\eta_E^{1/(m+1)}.
\tag{4}
\]
For small \(E\), a whole-circle image is excluded.  Continuous lifts and transverse averaging, followed by the one-dimensional Taylor interpolation inequality, give
\[
 \lVert D_{-i}T_i\rVert_\infty
 \leq C\operatorname {diam}(T_i)^{(k-1)/k}=o(1).
\tag{5}
\]
Uniform conditioning makes each diagonal derivative nonzero.  The homology matrix is diagonal with entries \(\pm1\).  After absorbing these isometries, the transverse average \(\phi_i\) is a circle diffeomorphism and
\[
 T_i(z)=\phi_i(z_i)+v_i(z),\qquad A_iv_i=0,\qquad\lVert v\rVert_\infty=o(1).
\tag{6}
\]
The sign of \(\det DT\) is constant.  If it is negative, composing with one additional coordinate reflection changes it to positive without changing either quotient loss or the absolute determinant residual.  Hence \(|\det DT|-1=\det DT-1\) in the normalized chart used below.

Compose by the uniformly conditioned coordinate maps so the coordinate part in (6) is the identity.  On the product boxes used in the strip-interpolation lemma, Taylor-expand \(v\) to degree \(k-1\).  The ratio equation has the exact divided-difference form
\[
 R_i(z_i+v_i)-R_i(z_i)
 =v_i\int_0^1R_i'(z_i+s v_i)\,ds,
\tag{7}
\]
and \(Q_i\) annihilates the arbitrary one-dimensional profile difference.  Retain the determinant equation exactly:
\[
 \det(I+Dv)-1=e_0.
\tag{8}
\]
On a noncritical box, (7) solves for the Taylor coefficients of \(v_i\).  On an \(i\)-critical strip, differentiating (8) transfers that coefficient to a component \(j\neq i\), where (7) solves it unless the box also meets a \(j\)-critical strip.  Uniform conditioning, (5), and determinant multilinearity bound all inverses in this finite coefficient elimination.  The divided differences in (7) and coefficient matrices in (8) differ from their linear parts by \(o(1)\); for small \(E\) their operator norm is at most one half, so they are absorbed on the left.

The adjacent-box transitions are (6)--(7) in the strip-interpolation proof.  Interior and periodic faces cancel, while \(A_iv_i=0\) removes the mixed field's coordinatewise kernel.  Only boxes meeting two critical strips retain a Taylor remainder.  Their cylindrical volume is \(O(h^2)\), so the \(C^k\) remainder contributes \(h^k h=h^{k+1}\).  Thus
\[
 \lVert v\rVert_2\leq C\{E/h^m+h^{k+1}\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Critical cardinality and separation make the number and overlap of boxes uniform.  This is an exact determinant calculation, not a Hodge correction.

It remains to control the coordinate part \(\phi\) by isometries.  The same coefficient elimination retains the degree-zero transverse averages from (8), rather than discarding them as the tangent lemma does.  To see its kernel explicitly, first put \(v=0\), set \(a_i=\log|\phi_i'|\), and use the positive orientation normalization.  The determinant equation becomes
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^n a_i(z_i)=\log\det D\phi(z).
\tag{10}
\]
Writing \(a_i=\bar a_i+a_i^\circ\), orthogonality under \(\lambda^n\) gives
\[
 \left\lVert\sum_i a_i\right\rVert_2^2
 =\sum_i\lVert a_i^\circ\rVert_2^2+\left(\sum_i\bar a_i\right)^2.
\tag{11}
\]
The degree condition is \(\int_{\mathbb T}\exp(a_i)\,d\lambda=1\).  Uniform derivative bounds and (11) consequently control each \(a_i\), and integration controls \(\phi_i\) modulo one rotation.  When \(v\neq0\), the Taylor coefficients involving \(Dv\) are exactly the coefficients already eliminated in (7)--(9); determinant multilinearity adds their controlled right side to (11).  Thus, for isometries \(I_i\) with the same signs and suitable rotations,
\[
 \left\{\sum_i\lVert\phi_i-I_i\rVert_2^2\right\}^{1/2}
 \leq C\{E/h^m+h^{k+1}\}.
\tag{12}
\]
Decoder and gauge conditioning uniformly bound the Jacobians of \(F_\theta\) and \(F_{\widetilde\theta}\).  Changing variables in the fixed-\(\lambda^n\) canonical loss through either map, and combining (9) with (12), therefore proves
\[
 d_Q(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq C\{E/h^m+h^{k+1}\}.
\tag{13}
\]
For \(0<E\leq h_0^{k+m+1}\), choose \(h=E^{1/(k+m+1)}\).  The two terms in (13) coincide.  Letting \(h\downarrow0\) handles \(E=0\), and bounded torus diameter handles larger \(E\).  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:canonical\text{-}encoder\text{-}invariance}\) gives \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\leq C d_Q\).

added_lemmas.statement:
For every aligned pair in \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Morse}}_{2,2,1}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\), the determinant residual and two Morse ratio residuals satisfy
\[
 d_Q(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
 \leq C\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)^{3/4}.
\]
After removal of coordinatewise fiber means, the mixed displacement obeys
\[
 \lVert v_{\rm mix}\rVert_2\leq C\{\mathcal E/h+h^3\}.
\]
Thus \(h=\mathcal E^{1/4}\) gives the exponent \(3/4\), uniformly over arbitrary bounded \(C^2\) torus diffeomorphisms in the primary class.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The primary Hessian assumption and Taylor's formula give, near each critical point,
\[
 |R_i'(z+u)|\geq(a_0/2)|u|.
\tag{1}
\]
Away from those neighborhoods, the finite-type profile gives the same form after changing the constant.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}type\text{-}incompressible\text{-}rigidity}\), with \(n=2,k=2,m=1\), therefore yields
\[
 \lVert v_{\rm mix}\rVert_2\leq C\{\mathcal E/h+h^3\}.
\tag{2}
\]
Its tangent coefficient system is the arbitrary-field system proved in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:primary\text{-}morse\text{-}weighted\text{-}divfree\text{-}coercivity}\), and its nonlinear proof retains \(\det DT-1\), rather than asserting \(\operatorname {div}v=0\).

For \(0<\mathcal E\leq h_0^4\), take \(h=\mathcal E^{1/4}\).  Then
\[
 \mathcal E/h=h^3=\mathcal E^{3/4}.
\tag{3}
\]
The comparison with both directed canonical losses proves the result.  Passage to the limit handles \(\mathcal E=0\); bounded torus diameter handles the remaining fixed range.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every fixed nondegenerate bounded class containing the Hamiltonian lower family, there are \(0<c\leq C<\infty\) and \(\varepsilon_0>0\) such that
\[
 c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}
 \leq\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)
 \leq C\varepsilon^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}
 \qquad(0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0).
\]
This records the previously established full-class bracket before applying determinant-assisted rigidity.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:lower\text{-}family\text{-}membership}\) and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:localized\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\) give
\[
 \Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\geq c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}
\tag{1}
\]
for small \(\varepsilon\).  The full-law residual reduction gives
\[
 \mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq C_0D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta).
\tag{2}
\]
For \(D_H\leq\varepsilon\leq C_0^{-1}\), scalar finite-type weak rigidity, with \(q=k/((k+n/2)(m+1))\), gives
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
 \leq C_1\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)^q
 \leq C_1C_0^q\varepsilon^q.
\tag{3}
\]
Taking the supremum in the inverse-modulus definition proves the bracket.

proposed.name: Canonical baseline encoder
proposed.construction:
Define the canonical baseline encoder by
\[
 g_\theta=\beta_\theta\circ h_\theta=F_\theta^{-1}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: This definition fixes the baseline probability-integral gauge before quotienting and is invariant under arbitrary latent coordinate changes up to isometry.

proposed.name: Intrinsic canonical-encoder quotient distance
proposed.construction:
Let \(\operatorname {Isom}(\mathbb T)\) be the rotations and reflections of the geodesic circle.  Define the fixed-reference orbit distance
\[
 d_Q(\theta,\widetilde\theta)=
 \inf_{\substack{\pi\in\mathfrak S_n\\ I_i\in\operatorname {Isom}(\mathbb T)}}
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb T^n}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \operatorname {dist}_{\mathbb T}\!\left(
 g_{\theta i}(y),I_i\!\left(g_{\widetilde\theta,\pi(i)}(y)\right)
 \right)^2d\lambda^n(y)\right\}^{1/2}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The canonical quotient needs a genuine compact isometry-orbit distance rather than the older discrepancy minimized over arbitrary coordinate diffeomorphisms.
The population functional is upgraded to the invariant canonical quotient while retaining the original modulus as an auxiliary comparison.
The probability-integral gauge supplies the requested invariant quotient representative; the older arbitrary-diffeomorphism loss remains auxiliary.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\Omega^Q_{k,m}(\varepsilon)=\sup_{D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq\varepsilon}d_Q(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\asymp\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\), uniformly on every fixed nondegenerate bounded class containing the lower family. The auxiliary modulus \(\Omega_{k,m}\) defined through \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\) has the same order. For \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), the exponent is \(3/4\).

The arbitrary-map strip-to-corner inequality now proves the sharp full-class modulus \(\Omega^Q_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\asymp\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\) for the intrinsic probability-integral-gauge encoder quotient, with the older \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\) retained only as an auxiliary aligned discrepancy. A finite certified spectral/spline procedure propagates the sharp modulus, giving primary representation rate \(N^{-3/16}\), and its permutation-compatible inverted law ball is honest with the same intrinsic quotient diameter.

project_justification.gap: Exact CauCA and score-change results do not quantify nonzero complete-law perturbations at isolated critical points, and prescribed-Jacobian or near-isometry rigidity does not supply the determinant-plus-degenerate-ratio inequality needed here.
project_justification.niche: Circular probability-integral gauges convert arbitrary latent reparameterizations into rotations or reflections, while paired interventions expose both the scalar profile residuals and a synthetic determinant channel. project_justification.fill: The note proves the synthetic product reduction, the arbitrary-field weighted coercivity estimate, nonlinear determinant absorption, the matching full-class inverse modulus, and the audited \(3/4\) Morse case. A deterministically enumerated rational periodic spline sieve carries interval certificates for positivity, normalization, DAG factorization, finite-type margins, decoder invertibility, and all unchanged class bounds. The fitting and calibration criteria minimize the empirical complete-law orbit distance over the finite common permutation group. Propagation through the sharp modulus yields \(\rho_N^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\); for \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), \(s_{\mathrm{obs}}=1\), so this is \(N^{-3/16}\).

prose_updates.related_work: Liang et al. and Varıcı et al. occupy exact componentwise recovery and plateau or almost-everywhere regimes, but neither supplies a nonzero-error full-law modulus. Buchholz and Schölkopf control a near-isometry defect rather than determinant distortion coupled to Morse-degenerate scalar transports. Prescribed-Jacobian and volume-correction results motivate the determinant channel, but the load-bearing strip-to-corner coefficient elimination is proved here directly and avoids an endpoint Hodge estimate. prose_updates.interpretation: The localized Hamiltonian family and the arbitrary-map upper inequality now meet. The dimension-free power is caused by two-coordinate critical corners: the \(C^k\) remainder contributes \(h^k\), their square-root volume contributes \(h\), and the order-\(m\) profile contributes the extra \(h^m\). Probability-integral canonicalization makes this a statement about an invariant quotient rather than a chosen latent gauge.

proofs.proof_tex:
For two labeled complete law families \(\mathbb Q=(Q^a:a\in\mathcal A)\) and \(\mathbb R=(R^a:a\in\mathcal A)\), define the fixed-label product Hellinger distance
\[
 \Delta(\mathbb Q,\mathbb R)^2
 =H^2(Q^{\mathrm{obs}},R^{\mathrm{obs}})
  +\sum_{i\in[n]}\sum_{e=0}^1 H^2(Q^{i,e},R^{i,e}).
\tag{1}
\]
If \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_n\), let \(\pi\mathbb Q\) leave the observational component fixed and put \((\pi\mathbb Q)^{i,e}=Q^{\pi^{-1}(i),e}\).  The well-typed empirical complete-law orbit distance appearing in Definition \(\mathrm{def:quotient\text{-}confidence\text{-}set}\) is
\[
 \widehat D_H(\theta,\widehat{\mathbb P}_L)
 :=\min_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_n}
       \Delta(\pi\mathbb P_\theta,\widehat{\mathbb P}_L).
\tag{2}
\]
The minimum in (2) is attained because \(\mathfrak S_n\) is finite.  Moreover, by the definition of Hellinger distance,
\[
 H(Q,R)=2^{-1/2}\lVert \sqrt{dQ/d\mu}-\sqrt{dR/d\mu}\rVert_{L^2(\mu)}
\]
for any common dominating probability measure \(\mu\).  Minkowski's inequality first in each \(L^2(\mu)\) coordinate and then in their finite Euclidean direct sum therefore gives
\[
 \Delta(\mathbb Q,\mathbb R)
 \leq \Delta(\mathbb Q,\mathbb S)+\Delta(\mathbb S,\mathbb R).
\tag{3}
\]
Thus no unproved metric property is being used below.

We next prove the deterministic comparison that makes the calibration permutation-compatible.  Fix \(\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\), and choose \(\pi_*\) attaining (2).  Common relabeling of the nodes preserves every defining condition of the model class, by Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:complete\text{-}grouping}\).  The \(\delta_N\)-net property and relabeling closure stipulated in Definition \(\mathrm{def:certified\text{-}spectral\text{-}estimator}\) consequently give a certified \(\vartheta_N\in\mathfrak M_N\) such that
\[
 \Delta(\pi_*\mathbb P_\theta,\mathbb P_{\vartheta_N})\leq\delta_N.
\tag{4}
\]
Indeed, the orbit net first gives a model within \(\delta_N\) after some common permutation, and closure of \(\mathfrak M_N\) under that permutation turns this into the fixed-label inequality (4).

Apply the defining \(\delta_N\)-approximate minimum-distance inequality to the candidate \(\vartheta_N\).  Equations (2)--(4) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Delta(\mathbb P_{\widehat\theta_N},\widehat{\mathbb P}_L)
 &\leq \Delta(\mathbb P_{\vartheta_N},\widehat{\mathbb P}_L)+\delta_N\\
 &\leq \Delta(\pi_*\mathbb P_\theta,\widehat{\mathbb P}_L)
       +\Delta(\pi_*\mathbb P_\theta,\mathbb P_{\vartheta_N})+\delta_N\\
 &\leq \widehat D_H(\theta,\widehat{\mathbb P}_L)+2\delta_N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
The permutation \(\pi_*\) is also an admissible alignment in Definition \(\mathrm{def:full\text{-}law\text{-}distance}\).  A further application of (3), followed by (5), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)
 &\leq \Delta(\pi_*\mathbb P_\theta,\mathbb P_{\widehat\theta_N})\\
 &\leq \Delta(\pi_*\mathbb P_\theta,\widehat{\mathbb P}_L)
       +\Delta(\widehat{\mathbb P}_L,\mathbb P_{\widehat\theta_N})\\
 &\leq 2\widehat D_H(\theta,\widehat{\mathbb P}_L)+2\delta_N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
This also shows that minimizing the fixed-label criterion over the relabeling-closed sieve has the same orbit-invariant consequence as minimizing the empirical orbit criterion.

Under Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}environment\text{-}sampling}\), Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:certified\text{-}spectral\text{-}law\text{-}recovery}\) supplies the uniform law-recovery rate used in the calibration.  By the calibration clause in Definition \(\mathrm{def:quotient\text{-}confidence\text{-}set}\), for fixed \(k,m\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \inf_{\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}}
 \Pr_\theta\!\left\{
   \widehat D_H(\theta,\widehat{\mathbb P}_L)
   \leq c_\alpha\rho_N
 \right\}
 \geq 1-\alpha-o(1).
\tag{7}
\]
On the event in (7), inequality (6) implies
\[
 D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)
 \leq 2c_\alpha\rho_N+2\delta_N.
\tag{8}
\]
The true \(\theta\) belongs to the displayed model class, so (8) makes \(\theta\) an admissible representing model in the defining set for \(\mathcal C_N(\alpha)\).  Hence
\[
 \left\{
   \widehat D_H(\theta,\widehat{\mathbb P}_L)\leq c_\alpha\rho_N
 \right\}
 \subseteq
 \left\{[h_\theta]\in\mathcal C_N(\alpha)\right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Taking probabilities in (9), then the infimum over \(\theta\), and finally using (7), proves
\[
 \inf_{\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}}
 \Pr_\theta\{[h_\theta]\in\mathcal C_N(\alpha)\}
 \geq1-\alpha-o(1).
\]
The argument uses the quotient only through common node relabeling and the reported encoder class; it does not infer equivalence of two encoders from vanishing of an auxiliary discrepancy.
